guideTitle: 6 Best Cordless Grass Shears Under $75 in 2026
metaDescription: Six cordless grass shears and hedge trimmer combos for edging and shaping, compared on blade size, battery type and weight so you can pick the right one.
introParagraphs: Cordless grass shears fill the gap between a string trimmer and a pair of hand clippers. They snip along fence lines, around flower beds and across the edges a mower cannot reach, and most of the models here swap to a small hedge blade in seconds. At this budget cap you can get a capable two-in-one tool, but the details differ more than the product photos suggest.

The main splits are battery type and blade length. Some tools use a small 7.2V pack that keeps weight down, others use a 21V pack or two of them for longer sessions, and one is a bare tool that borrows a DeWalt 20V battery you may already own. We evaluated each model on its listed specs and buyer feedback, paying attention to weight, adjustability and what actually ships in the box.

If your garden is a patio and a few shrubs, a compact tool will serve you better than a heavier one. If you have long hedges or a lot of edging, the larger battery options earn their extra heft. The guide below explains where each pick lands and where spending a little more would help.

products.name: WORKPRO 7.2V Cordless Grass Shear and Shrub Trimmer
products.description:
The WORKPRO is built around light weight. Its listing puts the tool at 0.82 lbs, with a 5.9 inch shrub trimmer blade and a 4.2 inch grass shear that swap in for each other. A 2.0Ah rechargeable battery powers an upgraded motor, and a safety lock prevents accidental starts.

The upside is easy handling, since you can hold it at arm's length for a long stretch of edging without tiring. The tradeoff is that a 7.2V tool has less cutting force than the 21V models, so thicker woody stems are not its job. It is best for grass edges, soft shrubs and light shaping.

Using it is simple: release the lock, hold the switch and let the blade work. Against the Sun Joe HJ604C at a listed 2.5 lbs, the WORKPRO is noticeably lighter, which suits smaller hands and longer sessions. It earns the top spot because it fits the most gardens without punishing the user.
products.bestFor: Small yards and light trimming where weight matters more than raw power.
pros: Listed weight of only 0.82 lbs
Two blades cover grass edges and shrubs
Safety lock prevents accidental starts
2.0Ah battery recharges between sessions
cons: 7.2V motor struggles with thick woody stems
Short blades mean more passes on long hedges

products.name: Sun Joe HJ604C 2-in-1 Cordless Grass Shear and Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
Sun Joe's HJ604C offers a one-touch exchange between a 4 inch grass shear and a 6 inch hedge trimmer blade. The 1250 RPM motor drives hardened steel blades that the maker says cut grass, small branches and woody stems without jamming. An ergonomic grip is meant to reduce wrist and shoulder fatigue.

Its selling point is the clean, fast blade change, which suits someone who jumps between edging and shrub shaping in the same session. It weighs 2.5 lbs by the listing, which is heavier than the compact WORKPRO. The same 7.2V power class also means it is not made for dense hedges.

As a handheld tool it needs little setup beyond charging and clicking a blade in. Compared with the Nicklaua at 1500 RPM, the Sun Joe runs a lower no-load speed but has the more recognized brand name and a simpler two-blade layout. It is a dependable middle choice.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who switch between edging and shaping and want a fast blade swap.
pros: One-touch swap between grass and hedge blades
Hardened steel blades are made for small stems
Ergonomic grip eases wrist and shoulder strain
Listed 1250 RPM motor drives a clean cut
cons: At 2.5 lbs it feels heavier than the WORKPRO
7.2V power will not handle dense branches

products.name: OGERY 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shears
products.description:
The OGERY steps up to a 21V platform and ships with two batteries, which lets you swap a spent pack for a fresh one mid-job. Its motor is listed at up to 2000 RPM, and the hedge blade is 8.9 inches long, so each pass covers more ground. It converts between hedge trimming and grass shearing like the others.

The second battery is the headline for anyone with a lot to trim. You can charge one while using the other, which stretches a session well beyond what a single small pack allows. The tradeoff is more tool weight and a bigger charging routine than the 7.2V options.

It asks a little more of the user in storage and charging, since two packs mean two things to keep topped up. Next to the Supleap at 600W, the OGERY gives you a stated motor speed and a spare battery, which makes its value easier to judge. Pick it for larger yards and longer hedges.
products.bestFor: Larger yards where a spare battery and a longer hedge blade save time.

8.9 inch hedge blade covers more per pass
Motor listed at up to 2000 RPM
Converts between hedge and grass heads
cons: Two batteries mean more charging to manage
Heavier to hold than the 7.2V tools

products.name: Nicklaua Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shears
products.description:
The Nicklaua uses a copper core motor rated at 1500 RPM no-load, with a 5.3 inch grass blade and a 9 inch hedge blade. Its head rotates to three angles, 15, 30 and 45 degrees, which helps when you are cutting across a flat edge or reaching into an awkward corner. The listing describes it as a battery-powered 2-in-1 tool.

Adjustable angles are the practical difference. They let you keep your wrist neutral while cutting the top of a low hedge or the edge of a lawn bed, which cuts down on awkward bending. The listing is less specific about battery details than the OGERY, so check what ships with it.

It is a neat choice for someone who values reach and angle over a recognizable brand. Compared with the Sun Joe HJ604C at 6 inches of hedge blade, the Nicklaua offers a longer 9 inch blade and a faster listed motor. Look at the battery section of the listing before ordering.
products.bestFor: People who value an adjustable head and longer hedge blade.
pros: Head rotates to 15, 30 and 45 degrees
9 inch hedge blade covers wider ground
Copper core motor listed at 1500 RPM

Lesser known maker than Sun Joe

products.name: Supleap 2-in-1 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The Supleap is a 21V tool rated at 600W with a battery that shows charge level on a display. Its double-sided high hardness blades adjust to multiple angles, and the body has an ergonomic anti-slip grip with shock absorption. It is described as a lightweight hedge and grass tool.

Comfort is its theme. The shock-absorbing grip and a visible charge indicator remove guesswork about how much working time is left. The tradeoff is that the listing gives fewer blade length figures than the others, so you have less to compare.

Expect it to behave like a mid-size trimmer, more robust than the 7.2V tools and lighter in the hand than a full hedge cutter. Against the OGERY at up to 2000 RPM, the Supleap lists power in watts instead, so the two are hard to compare directly. Choose it if the grip and the battery readout appeal to you.
products.bestFor: Users who want a visible battery readout and a cushioned grip.
pros: Battery display shows remaining charge

21V platform outpowers the 7.2V models
cons: Few blade length figures to compare

products.name: VERVEWAVE Cordless Hedge Trimmer for DEWALT 20V Battery
products.description:
The VERVEWAVE ships as a bare tool, with no battery or charger, and takes DEWALT 20V MAX lithium-ion packs. It carries two blades for quick changes between hedge trimming and grass shearing, and an upgraded copper-wire motor. The listing stresses that the battery and charger are not included.

That makes it a great value only for people who already own the batteries. If you have a DeWalt pack on a shelf, you add a trimmer without paying for another battery system. If you do not, the cost of a pack and charger can erase the saving, so it is not a good fit for first-time cordless buyers.

It is a third-party tool, not made by DeWalt, so warranty and support come from VERVEWAVE. Against the WORKPRO, which includes its battery, this one asks more of you at purchase but leaves you with a more interchangeable power source. It is the clear pick for existing DeWalt households.
products.bestFor: Owners of DEWALT 20V MAX batteries who want a trimmer without a new battery.

No new proprietary battery to buy

cons: Battery and charger are not included
Third-party tool, not made by DeWalt

buyingCriteria.explanation: Voltage sets how hard the tool can push through stems. The 7.2V group, including the WORKPRO 7.2V Cordless Grass Shear and Shrub Trimmer and the Sun Joe HJ604C, is best for grass, soft shrubs and light shaping. The 21V group, including the OGERY 21V Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shears and the Supleap, copes better with woody growth. Match the voltage to the thickest stem you expect to cut.

How the tool is powered shapes your whole routine. The OGERY ships with two 21V batteries, so you can swap a drained pack for a fresh one. The VERVEWAVE ships with none and takes DEWALT 20V MAX packs, which is a saving only if you already own them. Single 7.2V packs recharge faster but run out sooner on a big job.

Longer hedge blades cover more per pass, while shorter grass blades are better at tight edging. The Nicklaua Cordless Hedge Trimmer and Grass Shears pairs a 5.3 inch grass blade with a 9 inch hedge blade, and the OGERY offers 8.9 inches. The WORKPRO's 5.9 inch shrub blade and 4.2 inch grass shear are better for small beds. Pick the blade length that matches the length of your hedge.

Weight decides how long you can keep working before your wrist complains. The WORKPRO lists 0.82 lbs and the Sun Joe HJ604C lists 2.5 lbs, a threefold gap. Heavier 21V tools can feel more stable but tire the arm over a long session. If you have wrist or shoulder concerns, give weight more importance than power.

An adjustable head lets you cut flat edges, tops and corners without bending your wrist. The Nicklaua rotates to 15, 30 and 45 degrees, and the Supleap lists multi-angle blade adjustment. Fixed-head tools like the Sun Joe rely on moving your whole arm. For lawn edging at ground level, an adjustable head is worth having.

A two-in-one tool is only useful if you can change heads quickly. The Sun Joe HJ604C advertises a one-touch exchange between its 4 inch grass shear and 6 inch hedge trimmer. Others swap in seconds as well, but check how the head is released and locked. A tool that is awkward to convert tends to be used for only one job.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power class
howWeEvaluated.description: We grouped the tools into 7.2V, 21V and DEWALT-compatible classes. The WORKPRO and Sun Joe lead the light class, the OGERY and Supleap the 21V class, and the VERVEWAVE the shared-battery class. Each was judged against the job it is likely to be used for.

howWeEvaluated.title: Handling and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: Listed weight and grip design were compared. The WORKPRO's 0.82 lbs is the lightest figure, and the Supleap's anti-slip shock-absorbing grip is the most comfort-focused. Buyer feedback about wrist strain helped adjust the scores.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade coverage
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at blade lengths and head adjustability. The Nicklaua's 9 inch hedge blade and three head angles lead here. The Sun Joe's 6 inch blade and the WORKPRO's 5.9 inch blade are more suited to tight work.

howWeEvaluated.title: What is in the box
howWeEvaluated.description: Batteries and chargers affect true value. The OGERY includes two batteries, the WORKPRO includes one 2.0Ah pack, and the VERVEWAVE includes none. We marked down listings that were unclear about what ships.

howWeEvaluated.title: Everyday convenience
howWeEvaluated.description: Blade swaps, safety locks and charge indicators were compared. The Sun Joe's one-touch exchange and the Supleap's battery display stand out. We favored features that remove steps instead of adding them.

faq.q: Can these cordless grass shears cut thick branches?
faq.a: Not reliably. They are designed for grass, soft shrubs and thin stems. The 21V models like the OGERY and Supleap handle woody growth better than the 7.2V WORKPRO and Sun Joe, but none replaces a pruner or a full-size hedge trimmer. If the branch is thicker than a pencil, use loppers.

The WORKPRO 7.2V Cordless Grass Shear and Shrub Trimmer lists 0.82 lbs, which is the lightest figure. The Sun Joe HJ604C lists 2.5 lbs. Other listings do not give weight, so check the product page. A lighter tool is easier on the wrist for long sessions.

faq.q: Is the VERVEWAVE worth buying without a DeWalt battery?
faq.a: Usually not. It ships without a battery or charger, so you would need to buy both. The saving only appears if you already own DEWALT 20V MAX packs. Without them, a complete kit like the WORKPRO is simpler.

faq.q: How long does the battery last?
faq.a: Runtime depends on the pack and the load, and the listings give limited figures. Treat any runtime figure on a listing as a best case. A spare battery, as with the OGERY, is the surest way to extend working time. Cutting thick growth drains packs faster.

faq.q: Do I need a safety lock?
faq.a: It is a useful feature, since it stops the blades from starting by accident while you carry or swap the head. The WORKPRO lists a safety lock that is released after starting. Always remove the battery or switch off the tool before changing blades. Never rely on a lock alone.

faq.q: Can grass shears replace a string trimmer?
faq.a: For small areas and edges, yes, but not for large lawns. The shears give a cleaner cut on precise edges and are quieter. A string trimmer covers more ground faster. Many gardeners keep shears for the finishing touches.

faq.q: How should I store and maintain the blades?
faq.a: Wipe off sap and clippings after each use and keep the blades dry. A light coat of oil on the metal helps prevent rust. Store the tool with the battery removed, and charge the pack before long storage. Dull blades tear grass instead of cutting it, so replace or sharpen when the cut turns ragged.
